source_evidence: REACTIVE-AUDIT-2026-07-14 F3; five consecutive daily Priority 0c2 re-audits of the same change file chg-20260712-0010-003 (REACTIVE-AUDIT-2026-07-13 .. 2026-07-17, cycle 5 confirms current_verdict_holds=true each time)
problem: resolvePriorityAudit() uses c.audited_at on monitor/changes/*.json as the Priority 0c2 closure signal, but monitor/changes/ is append-only (writes to existing chg files are forbidden by the File Ownership rules) and 0 of 210 change files have ever been stamped. Every critical/strategic change therefore re-fires the 0c2 audit branch daily until the 7d natural cutoff, burning one redundant curmudgeon reactive-audit run per day per change (5 wasted cycles on chg-20260712-0010-003 alone). The class recurs with every future critical/strategic dome-site change.

options_considered.a_reactive_audit_coverage_scan: Dispatcher scans REACTIVE-AUDIT-*.json review files for chg-id references as the stamp-equivalent. No writes to changes/, no ownership-table changes, no new files. CHOSEN.
options_considered.b_claude_md_additive_edit_exception: Extend the append-only additive-edit exceptions to permit audited_at on chg files (popped_by_queue_id precedent). Rejected: requires CLAUDE.md + build.js + workspace-sync.md triple-edit (CLAUDE.md is NEVER_PUSH, would strand a patch), adds a fourth additive-edit exception for a problem solvable read-side, and the writer would be curmudgeon — a new write surface on an append-only dir.
options_considered.c_sidecar_files: monitor/changes/audited/chg-<id>.audited.json sidecars. Rejected: new write surface needing ownership classification, doubles file count in a 210-file dir over time, and the reviews dir already durably records exactly this fact.

proposed_fix.summary: In resolvePriorityAudit(), build a coverage set of chg ids referenced by completed REACTIVE-AUDIT-*.json reviews — union of (a) instrumentation.dispatcher_flagged_files basenames (field present since 2026-07-16, emitted from this same script's out.files) and (b) chg-\d{8}-\d{4}-\d{3} ids regexed from the audit's topic string (covers legacy audits that predate the instrumentation field; reactive-audit convention always names the audited chg id in topic). A change passing the classification+7d filters that is in the coverage set is counted in a new covered_by_reactive_audit_count observability field and skipped instead of firing 0c2. Failure-safe: unreadable reviews dir degrades to pre-fix re-fire behavior, never suppresses by error. The existing c.audited_at skip is preserved.

files_to_modify.find: resolvePriorityAudit() body: loop over monitor/changes/*.json with only `if (c.audited_at) continue;` as the audited check
files_to_modify.replace: Same loop preceded by an auditedChgIds Set built from monitor/curmudgeon/reviews/REACTIVE-AUDIT-*.json (dispatcher_flagged_files basenames + topic-string chg-id regex), with `if (auditedChgIds.has(f.replace(/\.json$/, ''))) { out.covered_by_reactive_audit_count++; continue; }` placed after the classification and 7d-cutoff filters so the counter only counts changes that would otherwise have fired; header doc block updated to document the stamp-equivalent semantics
files_to_modify.explanation: Applied in full in the same commit as this PROP (tinker self-apply per ISS-2986's explicit 'Design + implement ... (tinker judgment call)' assignment; PROP-136/ISS-2987 precedent). See commit diff for exact text.

tradeoffs: Gain: kills the daily 0c2 re-fire class at the read side with zero new write surfaces; one redundant Opus-class reactive-audit run saved per day per open critical/strategic change; observability via covered_by_reactive_audit_count. Lose/risk: (1) topic-regex matching could over-suppress if a future reactive-audit merely MENTIONS a chg id it did not actually audit in its topic — mitigated because reactive-audit convention puts only the audited chg id in topic, and the 7d cutoff already bounds any residual exposure; (2) an audit that crashed AFTER writing its review file would still count as coverage — acceptable, review files are written at completion; (3) deliberate re-audit of an already-covered change now requires a priority-queue item or human-note rather than relying on the daily re-fire — which is the correct routing anyway (the re-fires were adding no information: 5/5 cycles returned current_verdict_holds=true).
estimated_impact: ~1 redundant curmudgeon reactive-audit run avoided per day per open critical/strategic change (each a full Opus review cycle); dispatcher-state artifact now converges to the correct 0c2 state the day after the first audit lands instead of day 8.
